question: What defines a Class A commercial motor vehicle combination under the Connecticut CDL manual?
choice_a: Any vehicle designed to carry 16 or more passengers
choice_b: A GCWR of 10,000 pounds or more, regardless of the towed vehicle's weight
choice_c: A GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more for a single vehicle
choice_d: A GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than 10,000 pounds
explanation: The manual defines Class A Combination Vehicles as any combination with a GCWR of 26,001 or more pounds, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR, falls into which CDL vehicle class?
explanation: The manual states Class B Heavy Straight Vehicles are any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 or more pounds, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR less than 26,001 pounds is included in the CDL program as a Class C vehicle only if it meets which condition?
choice_b: It is used exclusively for farming operations
choice_c: It is designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or is used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding
choice_d: It is registered under the International Registration Plan
explanation: Class C vehicles (GVWR under 26,001 lbs) fall under the CDL program only if designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding under the Hazardous Materials Regulations.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: What is the minimum age to apply for a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) or obtain a CDL in Connecticut?
explanation: The manual states you must be at least 18 years of age to apply for a CLP and to obtain a CDL.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: According to the manual, what is the minimum age required to haul hazardous materials, drive interstate, or drive a school bus?
explanation: The manual lists 21 as the minimum age to haul hazardous materials, drive interstate, or drive a school bus.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: Before you may take any CDL/CLP knowledge test, what must you certify and provide proof of on your application?
choice_b: A valid International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA) license
choice_c: That you meet the physical qualification requirements of CFR Title 49, Section 391.41, in the form of a Medical Examiner's Report
choice_d: A completed hazardous materials background check
explanation: The manual requires applicants to certify on the CDL application, and provide proof via a Medical Examiner's Report, that they meet all physical requirements under CFR Title 49, Section 391.41, before taking any knowledge tests.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: A vehicle must have a CDL to operate if it is designed to transport how many passengers, including the driver?
explanation: The manual states a CDL is required for any vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as exempt from CDL requirements?
choice_d: Delivery vans with a GVWR over 26,001 pounds
explanation: The manual lists firefighting apparatus, along with authorized emergency vehicles, recreational vehicles, certain farm vehicles, and military vehicles operated by military personnel, as exempt from CDL requirements.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-1

question: Which three endorsements may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_b: Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank vehicle (N)
choice_c: Passenger (P), Hazardous Materials (H), and Tank vehicle (N)
explanation: The manual specifies that the only endorsements that may be added to a CLP are Passenger (P), School bus (S), and Tank vehicle (N).
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement is required for tanks meeting which capacity thresholds?
choice_a: Any tank regardless of size, if attached to a Class A vehicle
choice_b: An individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more
choice_c: An individual rated capacity of more than 1,000 gallons only
choice_d: An aggregate rated capacity of 500 gallons or more
explanation: The manual requires the N endorsement for tanks with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more, whether permanently or temporarily attached.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: A Passenger (P) endorsement is required for drivers of vehicles with a design capacity to carry how many people, including the driver?
explanation: The manual states drivers who wish to drive a vehicle with a design capacity of 16 or more people, including the driver, must add a Passenger endorsement.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Which agency requires a background check, including review of criminal, immigration, and FBI records, for drivers seeking a Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement?
explanation: The manual explains that the TSA and US DOT require background checks, including review of criminal, immigration, and FBI records, for drivers certified to transport hazardous materials.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-2

question: Which endorsement must a driver add to their CDL to haul hazardous materials or waste in a tank vehicle in amounts requiring placards?
choice_a: X - Combination Hazardous Materials and Tank Vehicle
explanation: The manual states drivers of tank vehicles who haul placarded hazardous materials or waste must add the X endorsement, showing they passed both the tank vehicle and hazardous materials knowledge examinations.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: What does restriction code E on a CDL indicate?
choice_a: The driver is restricted to intrastate commerce only
choice_c: The driver may not operate a CMV equipped with air brakes
choice_d: The driver is restricted from operating a CMV with a manual transmission because the skills test was passed in a vehicle with an automatic transmission
explanation: Restriction E applies when an applicant performs the skills test in a vehicle equipped with an automatic transmission, restricting the driver from operating a CMV with a manual transmission.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: What does restriction code K on a CDL indicate?
choice_a: The driver has been issued a medical variance
choice_b: The driver cannot operate a CMV with a manual transmission
choice_c: The driver cannot operate a CMV with air brakes
choice_d: The driver is restricted from operating a CMV in interstate commerce (intrastate only)
explanation: Restriction K applies when an applicant certifies Non-Excepted Intrastate or Excepted Intrastate status, restricting the driver from operating a CMV in interstate commerce.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: A driver who does not take or fails the air brake component of the knowledge test, or performs the skills test in a vehicle not equipped with air brakes, receives which restriction?
choice_a: O - restricted from operating a fifth-wheel connected CMV
choice_c: L - restricted from operating a CMV equipped with any type of air brakes
choice_d: E - restricted from operating a manual transmission CMV
explanation: The manual states restriction L applies when the air brake component of the knowledge test is not taken or failed, or the skills test vehicle lacks air brakes, restricting the driver from operating any CMV equipped with air brakes.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-3

question: Per the Connecticut CDL manual, a commercial driver's license expires within what period following the driver's next birthday?
choice_a: A period not to exceed four years
choice_b: A period not to exceed one year
choice_c: A period not to exceed two years
choice_d: A period not to exceed five years
explanation: The manual states a commercial driver's license shall expire within a period not to exceed four years following the date of the holder's next birthday.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-4

question: What must a CDL holder do to renew a hazardous materials endorsement, according to the manual?
choice_a: Pass the hazardous materials endorsement test within 6 months prior to renewal and submit fingerprints to the Transportation Security Administration
choice_b: Retake only the general knowledge test
choice_d: Obtain a new medical certificate only, with no retest required
explanation: The manual requires drivers renewing a hazardous materials endorsement to pass the hazmat endorsement test within 6 months prior to renewal and to submit fingerprints to the TSA before renewing.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-4

question: How long must a Connecticut CLP holder hold their permit before they may take the CDL skills test, per the manual?
explanation: The manual notes that you must hold a CLP at least 14 days before you may test for the CDL skills test.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: Which of the following is one of the CDL knowledge tests described in the manual?
choice_a: The air brakes test, required if your vehicle has air brakes, including air over hydraulic brakes
choice_b: The International Registration Plan compliance test
explanation: The manual lists the air brakes test as one of the CDL knowledge tests, required for anyone whose vehicle has air brakes, including air over hydraulic brakes.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-7

question: The CDL skills test consists of three segments that must be taken and passed in which order?
choice_a: On-road driving, vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control
choice_b: Basic vehicle control, on-road driving, vehicle inspection
choice_c: Vehicle inspection, on-road driving, basic vehicle control
choice_d: Vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, on-road driving
explanation: The manual states the CDL skills test consists of vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving, and each segment must be taken in that order and passed before moving to the next.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-8

question: A driver who operates in non-excepted interstate commerce must provide what to their State Driver Licensing Agency (SDLA)?
choice_a: A Commercial Learner's Permit renewal form
choice_b: Proof of International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA) registration
choice_c: A hazardous materials background check waiver
choice_d: A current medical examiner's certificate (DOT card)
explanation: The manual states drivers who operate in non-excepted interstate commerce must provide a current medical examiner's certificate under 49 CFR 391.45, commonly called a medical certificate or DOT card, to their SDLA.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-10

question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes it illegal to operate a commercial motor vehicle, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states it is illegal to operate a CMV if your blood alcohol concentration is .04% or more, and doing so results in losing your CDL for at least one year on a first offense.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-10

question: If a first-offense disqualifying violation (such as driving under the influence) occurs while operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials, how long is the CDL lost, per the manual?
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for at least three years if a disqualifying offense occurs while operating a CMV that is placarded for hazardous materials (a second offense results in a lifetime loss).
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-10

question: What happens under Connecticut CDL rules if a driver holds more than one commercial driver's license?
choice_a: It only results in a warning letter from the DMV
choice_b: It is allowed as long as one of the licenses is a CLP
choice_c: It is prohibited; a court may fine the driver up to $5,000 or jail them, keep the home state license, and return any others
choice_d: It is allowed if the licenses are from different states
explanation: The manual states you cannot have more than one license; breaking this rule can result in a court fine of up to $5,000 or jail, with the home state license kept and any others returned.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-12

question: According to the manual, how quickly must a driver notify their employer if their license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or if they are disqualified from driving?
explanation: The manual requires drivers to notify their employer within two business days if their license is suspended, revoked, or canceled, or if they are disqualified from driving.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-12

question: According to the manual, what is prohibited while operating a commercial motor vehicle in Connecticut?
choice_a: Adjusting the vehicle's mirrors while stopped
choice_c: Sending or reading text messages while driving
explanation: The manual states drivers are not allowed to send or read text messages while driving a CMV, and are also barred from holding a mobile phone to talk or dialing by pressing more than a single button.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-13

question: Per the manual, Individual Vehicle Distance Records (IVDR) supporting IRP and IFTA fees and taxes must be maintained for a minimum of how long?
explanation: The manual states the IVDR serves as the source document for calculating IRP/IFTA fees and taxes, and these original records must be maintained for a minimum of four years.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 1-14

question: How many questions are on the Connecticut CDL General Knowledge test, and how many correct answers are needed to pass?
explanation: The CT DMV's Commercial Learner's Permit overview states the General Knowledge test has 50 questions and requires 40 correct answers (80%) to pass.
source_note: Connecticut DMV, Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) overview, portal.ct.gov/dmv/commercial-and-industry-services/get-commercial-learners-permit (official CT.gov page, accessed 2026-08)

question: On the Connecticut Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement knowledge test, how many questions are given and how many must be answered correctly to pass?
explanation: The CT DMV's Commercial Learner's Permit overview states the Hazardous Materials endorsement test has 30 questions and requires 24 correct answers to pass.
source_note: Connecticut DMV, Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) overview, portal.ct.gov/dmv/commercial-and-industry-services/get-commercial-learners-permit (official CT.gov page, accessed 2026-08)

question: How many questions are on the Connecticut Air Brakes endorsement test, and how many correct answers are required to pass?
explanation: The CT DMV's Commercial Learner's Permit overview states the Air Brakes endorsement test has 25 questions and requires 20 correct answers to pass.
source_note: Connecticut DMV, Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) overview, portal.ct.gov/dmv/commercial-and-industry-services/get-commercial-learners-permit (official CT.gov page, accessed 2026-08)

question: According to the CT DMV's Commercial Learner's Permit overview, how is CDL knowledge and skills testing scheduled, and what is the general knowledge test fee?
choice_a: By appointment only at CT DMV offices; the general knowledge test fee is $16
choice_b: Walk-in only at any DMV office; the fee is $50
choice_c: Online only, with no in-person visit required; the fee is $10
choice_d: By mail-in application only; the fee is $25
explanation: The CT DMV's Commercial Learner's Permit overview states testing is offered by appointment only at CT DMV offices, and the general knowledge test fee is $16 (with each endorsement test at $5 and the skills test at $30).
source_note: Connecticut DMV, Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) overview, portal.ct.gov/dmv/commercial-and-industry-services/get-commercial-learners-permit (official CT.gov page, accessed 2026-08)
